findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — A successful Google refresh persists the safeParse wrapper instead of its data, so the next service construction rejects the stored credential and calendar operations fail.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Enabling user credential sync also applies the minimal parser to directly refreshed team credentials, stripping Office365 expiry and replacing its real refresh token with a placeholder that breaks subsequent refreshes.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — An otherwise valid Office365 response without its optional refresh token overwrites the previously retained token with the literal refresh_token, making the next refresh fail even with sync disabled.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — In sync mode this returns a fetch Response while the HubSpot caller still consumes a HubspotToken, so the parent API's JSON response yields undefined token fields and refreshes fail.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync endpoint returns a fetch Response but this caller reads the provider client's res.data shape, so parent-supplied tokens are never parsed and Google refreshes fail.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys both become "[object Object]", causing sync responses to strip expiry and token fields and breaking consumers that require their established token shape.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The new helper returns a Zod SafeParse result rather than credential data, and this stores { success, data } as the Google credential so later consumers cannot read access_token or expiry_date.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod SafeParse wrapper (`{success,data}`), and it is persisted as-is via `data: { key }`, so the stored credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails for every refreshed Google credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal "[object Object]", so `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is effectively `{access_token: string}` with all other keys (expiry, refresh_token, instance_url, etc.) stripped in credential-sync mode; the intended "any numeric property is expiry" rule never applies.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60 — If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the header is absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the secret check passes; the handler relies entirely on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (defined outside this diff) to gate that case.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:97 — findFirst` on `{userId, appId}` picks an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app (e.g. multiple Google accounts) and overwrites it; the update also never resets `invalid: false`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after fresh keys are synced.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — JSON.parse(req.query.state)` throws on a malformed state param, turning every callback that calls `decodeOAuthState` into an unhandled 500 rather than a graceful redirect.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys evaluate to literal property names rather than wildcards, so the shared sync schema silently stops enforcing its stated expiry-field contract and future integrations will rely on a misleading boundary.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The shared helper accepts and returns `any`, so its sync `Response` and provider token objects are indistinguishable to TypeScript and incompatible refresh handling can compile across every integration.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — This shared parser takes `any` and `ZodTypeAny`, so replacing provider schemas with the sync schema erases the credential shape at the OAuth boundary and lets incompatible persisted keys compile.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Salesforce duplicates the provider refresh fetch instead of using `refreshOAuthTokens`, leaving this newly added OAuth integration outside the credential-sync path and creating a second refresh implementation to maintain.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every SalesforceCalendarService construction refreshes and persists the token, adding a remote call and database write to each Salesforce calendar operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync path returns a raw Fetch Response although Google and HubSpot read provider token fields directly, so expired shared credentials fail to refresh and retry on each use.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The new parent credential-sync request has no timeout, so a stalled parent application can hold calendar and video refresh requests until runtime timeout.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, `undefined !== undefined` is false so any unauthenticated request can inject/overwrite credentials for any userId (unless APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived from the secret); add an explicit non-empty check.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Shared-secret comparison uses `!==` rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual, making it timing-sensitive.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:31 — Any accepted team member (not admin/owner) can install a team-level credential via an attacker-chosen `teamId` in the OAuth state; the throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam call at line 59 is only reached when teamId is absent and is therefore a no-op.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — Untrusted `req.query.state` is JSON.parse'd with no schema validation; malformed JSON throws an unhandled 500 and `teamId`/`returnTo` can be arbitrary types (e.g. object/string passed straight into prisma `where`).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret header/signature) and the parent app returns live access tokens for any calcomUserId, so the sync endpoint must be unauthenticated or rely on network trust; the response is also trusted unvalidated.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — When the provider omits refresh_token (normal for MS/Google refresh), the literal string "refresh_token" is injected and then merged/persisted (e.g. office365calendar CalendarService.ts:264), overwriting the user's real refresh token and permanently breaking the credential.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from `z.string().toString()` so it requires a nonsense key of type number and strips all real fields; with sync enabled every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens", and the schema does not actually validate the untrusted sync response.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — Decrypted payload is JSON.parse'd and written verbatim to credential.key with no per-app schema validation; symmetricDecrypt is called with "" when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, and both failures surface as unhandled 500s.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — Handler does not restrict HTTP method and calls `schema.parse` (throws) instead of safeParse, so GET/malformed bodies produce unhandled 500s with zod error details.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:98 — Error path redirects to raw `state.returnTo` without getSafeRedirectUrl, allowing open redirect from attacker-crafted state (pre-existing, but now routed through the shared decodeOAuthState helper).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The credential-sync validation branch has no test with a normal token payload, so the computed "[object Object]" required key can reject every refresh response and break token renewal.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — No refresh-path test asserts the Prisma credential payload, leaving the new SafeParse wrapper stored as `key` undetected and making the persisted Google credential unusable on its next read.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — The new webhook has no authentication test for an unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so requests with no header are accepted and can create or replace credentials.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The sync endpoint returns a fetch Response but this caller reads the provider client's res.data shape, so parent-supplied tokens are never parsed and Google refreshes fail.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: refreshOAuthTokens() in refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns either the result of refreshFunction() or a fetch Response from the sync endpoint. In GoogleCalendarService, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, the sync endpoint returns a raw fetch Response. The code then does `const token = res?.data` expecting the Google client's response structure (which has a .data property). A raw fetch Response doesn't have a .data property - you need to call res.json() first. So when credential sharing is enabled, `token` would be undefined, and `googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` would fail. This is a real bug where the two code paths return incompatible response types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys both become "[object Object]", causing sync responses to strip expiry and token fields and breaking consumers that require their established token shape.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The new helper returns a Zod SafeParse result rather than credential data, and this stores { success, data } as the Google credential so later consumers cannot read access_token or expiry_date.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 100 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (defined in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` - a Zod SafeParseReturnType object with `{success, data, error}` structure. This object is then stored directly as `key` in the credential update at line 101-104. However, the original code was `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returns the parsed data directly. So the new code stores the SafeParse result object instead of the actual credential data, which would break the credential storage.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the function returns `refreshTokenResponse` which is the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` - this is indeed a SafeParseResult object with `{success, data, error}` structure. In GoogleCalendarService.ts line 97, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` assigns this SafeParseResult directly to `key`, which is then stored via `data: { key }`. This would store `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of the actual credential data. The next time the credential is loaded and parsed with `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)`, it would fail because the structure doesn't match the expected schema. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — Computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal "[object Object]", so `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is effectively `{access_token: string}` with all other keys (expiry, refresh_token, instance_url, etc.) stripped in credential-sync mode; the intended "any numeric property is expiry" rule never applies.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. When you call `z.string().toString()`, it returns the string representation of the Zod schema object, which is '[object Object]' (or similar), not a dynamic key pattern. This means both computed keys resolve to the same literal string, and the schema doesn't actually validate 'any property with a number is the expiry' as the comment suggests. The minimumTokenResponseSchema will only properly validate `access_token` as a string, while the other 'dynamic' keys are incorrectly defined. This is a real bug - the intended schema behavior (allowing any numeric property as expiry) doesn't work as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60 — If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset and the header is absent, `undefined !== undefined` is false and the secret check passes; the handler relies entirely on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (defined outside this diff) to gate that case.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the secret check is: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined) and the header is also absent (undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` evaluates to `false`, meaning the check passes and the request is allowed through. However, the finding notes this relies on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED to gate the case - and indeed, lines 17-19 check `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) { return res.status(403)... }` which runs first. So if credential sharing is disabled, the endpoint returns 403 before reaching the secret check. The real question is: if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true but CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set, can an attacker bypass authentication? Yes - if the feature is enabled but the secret isn't configured, any request without the header would pass the check. This is a legitimate security concern - the secret check can be bypassed when the environment variable is not set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:97 — findFirst` on `{userId, appId}` picks an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app (e.g. multiple Google accounts) and overwrites it; the update also never resets `invalid: false`, so a credential previously marked invalid stays invalid after fresh keys are synced.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code uses `findFirst` with `{userId, appId}` to find credentials (lines 57-65). If a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), this would indeed pick an arbitrary one and update it, potentially overwriting the wrong credential. Additionally, the update operation (lines 68-75) only sets `key: keys` and does not reset `invalid: false`, so if a credential was previously marked invalid, it would remain invalid even after receiving fresh keys. Both issues are real problems visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys evaluate to literal property names rather than wildcards, so the shared sync schema silently stops enforcing its stated expiry-field contract and future integrations will rely on a misleading boundary.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 7-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as property keys. This is a misunderstanding of how Zod works - `z.string().toString()` returns a string representation of the Zod schema object (like '[object Object]' or similar), not a dynamic key pattern. Zod doesn't support dynamic/wildcard keys this way. The intended behavior of matching 'any property with a number' for expiry and allowing other optional properties won't work as expected. This creates a schema that has literal computed property names rather than the intended flexible matching, which means the validation won't properly enforce the expiry field requirement. This is a real bug in the schema definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The shared helper accepts and returns `any`, so its sync `Response` and provider token objects are indistinguishable to TypeScript and incompatible refresh handling can compile across every integration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the function signature is `async (refreshFunction: () => any, appSlug: string, userId: number | null)` and returns `any`. The finding correctly identifies that this uses `any` types, which means TypeScript won't catch type mismatches between different OAuth providers' response formats. However, this is more of a type safety/code quality concern rather than a concrete bug. The code will still function correctly at runtime - it's just that TypeScript won't provide compile-time guarantees. The finding describes a real typing weakness that could lead to bugs, but it's borderline between a legitimate defect and a code quality/style issue. Given that using `any` in a shared utility that handles different OAuth providers' responses could mask real type errors, this is a legitimate concern about correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — This shared parser takes `any` and `ZodTypeAny`, so replacing provider schemas with the sync schema erases the credential shape at the OAuth boundary and lets incompatible persisted keys compile.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the parseRefreshTokenResponse function in the diff, it takes `response: any` and `schema: z.ZodTypeAny`. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the passed schema. The function returns `refreshTokenResponse` which could be either the result of the minimum schema or the passed schema. However, the finding claims this 'erases the credential shape at the OAuth boundary and lets incompatible persisted keys compile' - but this is about runtime behavior, not compile-time type safety. The function does have a type safety issue (using `any` and `ZodTypeAny`), but the actual problem described - that it would let incompatible keys be persisted - is speculative. The code does validate against either the minimum schema or the passed schema, and throws if validation fails. The real issue is that when credential sharing is enabled, it uses a looser schema, but this appears to be intentional design for the credential sync feature. The finding is somewhat valid about type looseness but overstates the actual defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The sync path returns a raw Fetch Response although Google and HubSpot read provider token fields directly, so expired shared credentials fail to refresh and retry on each use.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, refreshOAuthTokens returns either the result of the external fetch (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) or the result of refreshFunction(). In GoogleCalendarService, the code does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` then `const token = res?.data`. For the sync path, the fetch returns a Response object which doesn't have a `.data` property - it would need `await response.json()` first. However, looking at the Google implementation, the refreshFunction returns `fetchTokens.res` which is the googleapis response object that has `.data`. For the sync endpoint path, it returns a raw fetch Response, and accessing `res?.data` on a fetch Response would be undefined, causing `token.access_token` to fail. This is a real bug - the sync path returns incompatible data structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The new parent credential-sync request has no timeout, so a stalled parent application can hold calendar and video refresh requests until runtime timeout.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, the fetch call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT at line 8-14 indeed has no timeout configuration. The fetch API in Node.js doesn't have a default timeout, so if the external endpoint is slow or unresponsive, the request could hang indefinitely. This is a real issue - when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and the credential sync endpoint is configured, calendar refresh operations (Google Calendar, Office365, Lark, etc.) would all go through this code path and could be blocked by a stalled external service. This is a legitimate concern for production reliability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, `undefined !== undefined` is false so any unauthenticated request can inject/overwrite credentials for any userId (unless APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived from the secret); add an explicit non-empty check.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the webhook secret check is: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` evaluates to `false`, meaning the check passes and the request is authenticated. This allows unauthenticated requests to inject/overwrite credentials for any userId when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true but CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured. This is a real security vulnerability - the code should explicitly verify that CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set and non-empty before comparing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Shared-secret comparison uses `!==` rather than crypto.timingSafeEqual, making it timing-sensitive.

Using `!==` instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual makes the comparison vulnerable to timing attacks, where an attacker could potentially determine the secret character by character by measuring response times. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The credential-sync validation branch has no test with a normal token payload, so the computed "[object Object]" required key can reject every refresh response and break token renewal.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed property keys. When you call `z.string().toString()`, it returns a string representation of the Zod schema object (likely '[object Object]' or similar), not a dynamic key pattern. This is a fundamental misunderstanding of how Zod works - Zod doesn't support dynamic/wildcard keys this way. The schema would require literal keys matching whatever `z.string().toString()` evaluates to, which would cause validation to fail for normal token responses that have keys like 'expires_in', 'refresh_token', etc. This is a real bug that would break token renewal when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — No refresh-path test asserts the Prisma credential payload, leaving the new SafeParse wrapper stored as `key` undetected and making the persisted Google credential unusable on its next read.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 97 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 98-100 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function returns a SafeParseReturnType object (with .success and .data properties), not the actual credential data. This means the entire SafeParse result object is being stored as the key, not just the parsed data (refreshTokenResponse.data). This is a real bug - the code should be storing `key.data` or handling the parse result properly, but instead stores the wrapper object, which would make the credential unusable on next read.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — The new webhook has no authentication test for an unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, so requests with no header are accepted and can create or replace credentials.
